description: Component upgrade lifecycle for the AI platform. This file lives on the `lifecycle` branch
(the GitHub default branch, so Renovate reads it from here) and targets `main` only.
`main` carries NO Renovate annotations: every pin is found by the managers below, keyed on
the shapes that exist on `main` today. tests/test_renovate_coverage.py (run weekly against
`main` by .github/workflows/coverage.yaml) fails when a pin stops matching.
PRs are grouped by UPGRADE DOMAIN, each anchored on the component whose version gates the
infra      - anchored on the EKS Kubernetes version (Karpenter, LBC, KEDA, TF modules/providers, k8s clients)
inference  - anchored on the vLLM image (gpu-operator, GIE CRDs, llm-d router, s5cmd, prometheus)
gateway    - LiteLLM and what talks to it (postgres, langfuse, open-webui, oauth2-proxy, python libs)
tooling    - GitHub Actions + CI tool versions
The Kubernetes version itself (cluster_config.kubernetes_version) is deliberately NOT managed
here: anchor bumps are human commits that follow the EKS support calendar. EKS managed addons
are converged by Terraform most_recent=true and reported by addon-freshness on `main`.
Merge policy: nothing automerges and Renovate PRs into `main` are never merged directly; their
branches are merged into a `release/<version>` branch, validated by E2E, and released together.
Majors and anchors need a tick on the Dependency Dashboard before a branch is even created.

customManagers.description: Helm charts declared in the ArgoCD platform ApplicationSet (chart / chartRepo / chartVersion triplets).

vLLM serving image default baked into the KRO serving-tier schemas (VLLMEndpoint, LLMDEndpoint, LLMDDisaggEndpoint). Must track terraform/30.eks/30.cluster/locals.tf vllm_image_tag; same group so they move together.
llm-d router Helm chart (OCI, ghcr.io/llm-d/charts) default in the LLMD* KRO schemas.
Python base image used by the Platform Health Agent's spawned Jobs (a ConfigMap value, not an image: field).

Inline 'pip install name==version' pins inside init containers (litellm-sync, cluster-dashboard, PHA event-watcher) AND inside the Job specs the dashboard/PHA Python builds at runtime (backend.py, event_watcher.py). Those Jobs run on PYTHON_IMAGE, so a python bump needs wheels for these pins.
vLLM serving image tag, single source of truth in the cluster stage locals (vllm_image_tag = "<v>"). Same dep as the RGD defaults, so both move in one PR.
AWS Load Balancer Controller chart: chart_version = "<v>" inside the aws_load_balancer_controller block of the blueprints addons module.
Python CI tools pinned inline in workflow run steps (`pip install [flags] name==v name==v ...`). Recursive: first the pip line, then each name==version on it.

packageRules.description: Default: every Terraform provider/module is infra (control-plane adjacent). Later rules override for specific deps.
infra domain - anchored on the EKS Kubernetes version. Karpenter chart<->CRD<->k8s window, LBC v3 (CRDs applied separately + IAM supplement), KEDA, k8s clients.
k8s Python client must stay within +/-1 minor of the API server (kubernetes-client policy). Current anchor k8s 1.36 -> client 31..33 OK; raise the ceiling when bumping kubernetes_version.
alpine/k8s bundles kubectl; keep within +/-1 minor of the API server (kubectl skew policy). Raise with the anchor.
inference domain - anchored on the vLLM image. GPU operator driver/CUDA >= vLLM's CUDA runtime; GIE CRDs + llm-d router must match the vLLM routing protocol.
gateway domain - LiteLLM and everything that talks to it. Postgres major = dump/restore; Langfuse chart v2->v3 = ClickHouse data-store migration.
gitops domain - the engine that applies everything else (self-managed ESC path; managed capabilities are AWS-owned).
tooling domain - CI only, no cluster impact.
Anything found in a GitHub workflow is CI-only, whatever its dep name (python, pyyaml, kubernetes... also exist cluster-side). File-based so it overrides the dep-name groups above.
LiteLLM publishes '-stable' tags; only follow those, never nightlies.
Majors anywhere: a human ticks the checkbox on the Dependency Dashboard before the PR is opened.
Anchors: any change (even a patch) is reviewed deliberately, so never automerge and always surface on the dashboard.

The github-actions manager also reads setup-terraform's terraform_version (depName 'terraform'). The regex manager above owns that pin (depName hashicorp/terraform, same as the terraform manager), so disable the built-in copy to avoid two PRs for one line.
